user.title: Protect energy sensors
user.description:
Energy Guard creates protected copies of cumulative energy sensors. A protected sensor never publishes a reconnect artefact (unavailable, unknown or a false 0) - it publishes 'unavailable' instead, so the Energy Dashboard statistics, utility meters and cost history stay correct.

Select one or more cumulative energy sensors (device_class: energy, state_class: total_increasing). {count} matching sensors were found. You can add derived sensors later in the options.

data_description.source_entity_id: Every selected sensor gets its own protected sensor (for example sensor.grid_import_protected).

naming.title: Name the protected sensors
naming.description: These names become the entity ids of the protected sensors. Sources: {sources}

detection.title: Detection thresholds
detection.description: The defaults are safe for typical energy meters. {sensors} protected sensor(s) will be created. Everything can be changed later in the options flow.

data_description.scan_interval: How often the read-only scan checks the recorder for suspicious offsets. 300 seconds (5 minutes) is a good balance.
data_description.lookback_hours: How far back each scan looks. 24 hours catches overnight outages.
data_description.issue_window_hours: Only anomalies inside this window count towards the issue sensor and the Repairs issues.
data_description.simultaneous_threshold: How many different sensors must fail inside the window before a simultaneous failure is reported.
data_description.simultaneous_window_minutes: Time window in which several failures count as one simultaneous event (a shared gateway or power problem).
data_description.event_retention_days: How long diagnostic events are kept in the log before they are pruned.

init.title: Energy Guard options
init.description:
Manage everything Energy Guard creates. {protected} protected sensor(s), {derived} derived sensor(s), {meters} utility meter(s), {issues} open issue(s).

Energy Guard only manages its own entities and configuration. It never reads or edits your YAML/template files.

protected_sensors_add.description: Create a protected copy of a cumulative energy sensor. Advanced thresholds can be left at their defaults.

data.name: Name
data.accept_real_reset: Accept a confirmed real meter reset
data.confirm_scans: Readings needed to confirm a reset
data.recovery_hold_scans: Readings to wait after a reconnect

data_description.name: Becomes the entity id (spaces turn into underscores). Keep the ' protected' suffix so the source and the copy are easy to tell apart.
data_description.source_entity_id: The cumulative energy sensor to copy. It must report device_class energy and state_class total_increasing.
data_description.unit_of_measurement: Unit of the protected sensor. Values are converted from the source unit automatically.
data_description.offset: Constant added to every reading, in the unit above. Use it to continue an old total after a meter replacement.
data_description.enabled: Disabled sensors are not created; their definitions and history are kept.
data_description.do_not_decrease: When enabled, a decrease is held back (published as unavailable) instead of being accepted as a meter reset.
data_description.accept_real_reset: Only enable this if your meter can legitimately jump back to 0 (meter replacement). The reset must then be confirmed by repeated readings.
data_description.zero_min_previous: A 0 is only treated as suspicious when the last good value was at least this high.
data_description.confirm_scans: How many consecutive readings must confirm a reset before it is accepted (only used together with 'Accept a confirmed real meter reset').
data_description.recovery_hold_scans: Number of readings that must be sane after a reconnect before values are published again.
data_description.grace_period: Gaps shorter than this are not treated as a reconnect.
data_description.large_jump: A single reading jump larger than this (in the unit above) is treated as suspicious.
data_description.large_jump_ratio: A jump is also suspicious when it is this many times larger than the typical increase between readings.
data_description.reject_large_jumps: When enabled, a suspicious jump is held back (published as unavailable) instead of accepted.
data_description.precision: Decimals shown for the state. The statistics keep full precision.
data_description.max_value: Readings above this are held back. Leave empty when the meter has no known plausible maximum.

derived_sensors.title: Derived Sensors
derived_sensors.description:
{count} derived sensor(s): {items}

Derived sensors calculate sums, differences or phase splits from other energy sensors and apply the same protection.

derived_sensors_add.description: Sum: adds all selected sensors. Difference: first sensor minus the others. Phase split: total minus the phase sensors.

utility_meters.title: Utility Meters
utility_meters.description:
{count} utility meter(s): {items}

Energy Guard does not create utility meters. It stores which protected sensor belongs to which utility meter so that energy_guard.calibrate_utility_meter can calculate the correct value automatically.

detection_rules.description: How often the read-only statistics scan runs and when issues are reported.

data_description.scan_interval: How often the read-only scan checks the recorder for suspicious offsets. 300 seconds (5 minutes) is a good balance.
data_description.lookback_hours: How far back each scan looks. 24 hours catches overnight outages.
data_description.issue_window_hours: Only anomalies inside this window count towards the issue sensor and the Repairs issues.
data_description.simultaneous_threshold: How many different sensors must fail inside the window before a simultaneous failure is reported.
data_description.simultaneous_window_minutes: Time window in which several failures count as one simultaneous event (a shared gateway or power problem).
data_description.event_retention_days: How long diagnostic events are kept in the log before they are pruned.

statistics_repair.title: Statistics Repair
statistics_repair.description:
Thresholds used by the read-only scanner ({candidates} candidate(s) in the last scan, last scan: {last_scan}).

Scanning never changes data. Repairs only happen when you call energy_guard.repair_statistics with confirm: true.

data_description.statistics_jump_threshold: An hourly statistics increase above this value is reported (in kWh).
data_description.statistics_jump_ratio: A jump is also reported when it is this many times larger than the typical hourly increase.
data_description.scan_scope: Which statistics the scanner covers by default. 'Only my Energy Guard sensors' keeps scans fast (protected sources, derived sensors, utility meter sources and the cost statistics). 'All energy statistics' also checks every other energy sensor in the recorder, including ones not managed by Energy Guard. 'All statistics' checks every cumulative statistic whatever its unit. Scanning is always read-only; nothing is repaired automatically.
data_description.sum_state_ratio: A statistic is also reported when its recorded sum is this many times larger than the state history says it should be.

cost_repair.title: Cost Repair
cost_repair.description: Settings used to translate a repaired energy offset into a monetary correction. Cost repairs always need their own confirmation (confirm_cost: true).

data_description.price: For example 0.235 for 0.235 GEL per kWh.
data_description.energy_statistic_id: The statistic that contains the false kWh offset (for example sensor.grid_import).
data_description.cost_statistic_id: The cost statistic created by the Energy Dashboard (for example sensor.grid_import_cost).
data_description.enabled: When off, scans skip the monetary math and no cost suggestions are shown.
data_description.currency: Currency code of the tariff, for example GEL, USD or EUR. Only used for display.
data_description.price_entity_id: Optional: a sensor with the live price per kWh. When set, it is used instead of the fixed tariff above.

statistics_offset.title: Energy Guard found {count} suspicious statistics offset(s)
statistics_offset.description:
The recorder statistics of **{statistic_id}** show a change of {offset} {unit} at {start_time} that does not match the recorded state history. This is the classic signature of a reconnect (unavailable -> 0 -> lifetime value) that was written before Energy Guard was installed.

Nothing was changed. Run `energy_guard.scan_statistics` to review the evidence, then `energy_guard.repair_statistics` with `confirm: true` to apply the suggested offset (a JSON backup of every changed statistic is written first).

blocked_readings.title: {count} bad energy reading(s) blocked in the last {window_hours} h
blocked_readings.description:
**{integration} {version}** suppressed {count} reading(s) of {entities} that would have corrupted the Energy Dashboard (an estimated {estimated_false_energy} kWh of false energy).

The protected sensors stayed `unavailable` instead of publishing a false 0, so no new corruption was written. Check your meter or gateway if the source sensors keep reconnecting, and use `energy_guard.scan_statistics` to find older damage.
